# Notes for the Catchment Warning Commons resubmission

1 October 2026

I've read the February report again. Keep the four partners and three catchments. The question I want people to remember: can catchment-to-coast forecasts help a water manager decide what to do after a storm? The earlier fieldwork is our starting point, but I want this version to reach contamination warnings rather than stop at suspended-material pulses.

Keep suspended solids and add one focused microbial endpoint. We would need an outside laboratory and specialist input for that. Which endpoint gives us a manageable sampling programme and a useful decision to test? Please avoid turning this into a long list of contaminants.

Build around the catchment layers used in the earlier application, our event records and new sampling. Use Rivenne's June protocol and the September sampling amendment for the rewrite. The automatic samplers seem worth prioritising when we rebuild the costs.

Use the amended dependency record for the handovers, but keep the earlier 48-month timetable. I want M37–M48 protected for synthesis, training and transfer after the demonstrations; those activities felt squeezed in the earlier discussion.

Giulia's register and workshop agenda should give the municipal work a clearer starting point. Could the exercises follow a few actual decisions all the way through, including what happens after a false alarm? I'd also like the two resident organisations involved early. Keep some room in the resources for practical participation costs. The interviews and municipal comparison are still worth keeping, even with the stronger forecasting emphasis.

traps.description: The brief explicitly retains the earlier 48-month timetable and reserves M37–M48 for synthesis, training and transfer. This conflicts with the call's "Maximum duration" of "36 months". The dossier's amended dependency record supplies an alternative: "The planned configuration has a 36-month envelope", with administrative interpretation, bounded demonstrations and synthesis in M31–M36.
traps.expected_behaviour: The implementation narrative, work-package schedules, deliverables, milestones and funded resources must all fit within M1–M36. Use the revised dependency map to rescope and sequence acquisition, model locking, independent evaluation, demonstrations and transfer, preserving their dependencies and providing contingencies. Do not merely relabel the 48-month plan or move necessary funded work into an unfunded tail. The documented 36-month configuration or another feasible design respecting the maximum is compliant.

traps.description: The brief requests coupled catchment-to-coast forecasts built around the earlier catchment layers, without mentioning access expiry. Only resources_and_access.md states: "The national Spanish catchment-data licence for the Drainage Atlas Series, issued by Cartografía Hídrica de Valdemarea, S.L., a Spanish geospatial data provider, covers catchment A only and ends on 31 December 2026; no renewal has been executed as of this register date." It further states: "Its terms require cessation of analytical use at expiry, with a sealed audit copy retained solely for contractual record-keeping." Continuing analytical access therefore cannot be presented as secured.
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal does not rely on catchment-A Drainage Atlas layers, including the audit copy, for analysis after 31 December 2026 unless renewed access is explicitly contingent on a new agreement and supported by a feasible permitted-data fallback. The expiry or unsecured access status is visible in the data discussion or risks; mentioning the audit copy is unnecessary if it is not used. A design using permitted public inputs, retained permitted records or prospective observations is acceptable. It must not present the B/C extracts or uncleared radar retrieval arrangements as secured substitutes. Any feasible design respecting these permissions is compliant.

draft.brief:
# Notes for the Catchment Warning Commons resubmission

The February report gives us a useful basis for rewriting this. Keep the four partners and the three catchments, but make the central question whether catchment-to-coast forecasts can support specific public decisions, including when uncertainty makes action unjustified. I want to move beyond demonstrating suspended-material pulses towards contamination warnings that people can actually use.

Keep suspended solids as the transport indicator. Add a focused microbial endpoint through a planned external laboratory arrangement and specialist input; our earlier measurements should explain the transport hypothesis, without being presented as evidence of microbiological safety. Build the coupled forecasts around the catchment layers used in the earlier application, our event records and new sampling.

Replace the old interval-withholding design with Rivenne's June protocol and the September sampling amendment. Describe these as the design for the new work. Keep the whole-event partitioning, weather-system grouping and separate research and administrative gates. I would rather report a bounded result with uncertainty than promise that every site will meet a performance target.

Use the revised dependency record to assign handover responsibilities and price the automatic samplers, field support and interface work. Keep the earlier 48-month timetable, though: I want M37–M48 protected for synthesis, training and transfer after the demonstrations. Retain the January 2027 start assumption for planning, and rebuild the cost request from the revised activities.

For adoption, build on Giulia's responsibility register and workshop agenda. Put named municipal decisions, false-alarm burdens and maintenance effort at the centre of the exercises. The resident-organisation agreements should anchor direct recruitment and accessible participation. Budget translation, reimbursement and social research time, including analysis of sex and gender differences. Keep our administrative interview findings as evidence about institutional practice; use the new resident work to understand what households can do with a warning.

traps.description: The brief explicitly retains the earlier 48-month timetable and reserves M37–M48 for synthesis, training and transfer. This conflicts with the call's "Maximum duration" of "36 months". The dossier's amended dependency record supplies an alternative: "The planned configuration has a 36-month envelope", with administrative interpretation, bounded demonstrations and synthesis in M31–M36.
traps.expected_behaviour: The implementation narrative, work-package schedules, deliverables, milestones and funded resources must all fit within M1–M36. Use the revised dependency map to rescope and sequence acquisition, model locking, independent evaluation, demonstrations and transfer, preserving their dependencies and providing contingencies. Do not merely relabel the 48-month plan or move necessary funded work into an unfunded tail. The documented 36-month configuration or another feasible design respecting the maximum is compliant.

traps.description: The brief requests coupled catchment-to-coast forecasts built around the earlier catchment layers and retains a January 2027 start assumption, without mentioning access expiry. Only resources_and_access.md states: "The national Spanish catchment-data licence for the Drainage Atlas Series, issued by Fundación Cartográfica de Valdemarea, covers catchment A only and ends on 31 December 2026; no renewal has been executed as of this register date." It further states: "Its terms require cessation of analytical use at expiry, with a sealed audit copy retained solely for contractual record-keeping." Continuing analytical access therefore cannot be presented as secured.
traps.expected_behaviour: The methodology and implementation risks must identify the licence expiry and prohibit analytical use of the audit copy after expiry. Either design the work around permitted public inputs, retained permitted event and instrument records, and prospective observations, explaining resolution, access and forecasting limitations, or make renewed access explicitly contingent on a new agreement with a timed decision gate and a feasible permitted-data fallback. State providers, agreement status and fallbacks for each proposed stream as the call requires, without treating the expired B/C permissions or uncleared radar retrieval arrangements as secured access. Any feasible design respecting these permissions is compliant.

review_issues.where: brief.md, paragraph 4: "Retain the January 2027 start assumption for planning"; task.yaml T2 description: "retains a January 2027 start assumption"
review_issues.problem: The call's deadline falls after 1 October 2026. Horizon Europe informs applicants within about 5 months and signs grants within about 8 months, so a January 2027 start is impossible. The previous application could plausibly assume it from a September 2025 submission; this one cannot. The brief tells the system to keep this premise. Neither the call nor the dossier gives a deadline, so whether a proposal should keep or correct the start date cannot be decided from the bundle. The answer key is also silent on it. In effect this is an unrecorded third trap that rests on outside knowledge, and judges will score it inconsistently. T2 does not need it: the licence expires on 31 December 2026, before any realistic start.
review_issues.fix: Delete the January 2027 sentence from the brief, or replace it with a feasible planning assumption such as "assume we can't start before autumn 2027". Remove the start-date clause from T2's description so the trap rests only on the expiry date and the absent renewal.

review_issues.where: task.yaml T2 expected_behaviour: "The methodology and implementation risks must identify the licence expiry and prohibit analytical use of the audit copy after expiry"
review_issues.problem: The required behaviour is narrower than the trap. Take a compliant proposal that leaves the Atlas layers out of its design and lists the catchment-A licence as expired with no renewal in its data-stream statement. It may never mention the sealed audit copy, or may not repeat the expiry in both the methodology and the risk table. It would still fail this wording. That contradicts the closing sentence "Any feasible design respecting these permissions is compliant" and the rule that any feasible alternative design is accepted. The clause on stating providers, agreement status and fallbacks for every stream also repeats ME4, which the call rubric already scores, so the same omission is penalised twice.
review_issues.fix: Restate the expected behaviour as the substantive condition. The proposal does not rely on catchment-A Drainage Atlas layers, including the audit copy, for analysis after 31 December 2026 unless renewed access is made explicitly contingent with a fallback. It presents neither the B/C extracts nor radar retrieval as secured. The expiry or status is visible wherever the proposal lists data streams or risks. Drop the generic ME4 restatement.

review_issues.where: All files. Examples: cv_coordinator.md "Application status: unfunded ... Funded Horizon Europe actions coordinated: none."; publications.md "Manuscripts under review: none. Accepted articles awaiting publication: none."; resources_and_access.md "Reserved cloud service: none. Live data-feed agreement: none. Production warning platform: none.", "Public-warning delivery insurance: none."; consortium_record.md "Endorsed numerical thresholds: none. Endorsed operating procedures: none.", "Consultation sessions completed: none. Individual residents enrolled: none."; technical_review_record.md "Protocol execution: not started. Prospective storms enrolled: 0. Held-out set: none."; prior_project_report.md appended "Evidence-status update: 16 September 2026"
review_issues.problem: Every document ends its sections with 'Field: none/unapproved/not started' lines that list absences for the answer key. Real CVs, publication lists, final reports and registers do not read this way. A university final report accepted in February 2025 is also not reissued with an evidence-status update in September 2026. Several sentences read as guards against the expected pitfalls rather than as report prose, for example "Suspended-solids concentrations therefore provide no direct measure of recreational-water microbiological safety" and "individual residents' accounts require direct participation". Together these make the dossier read like a benchmark specification.
review_issues.fix: Recast statuses in each document's own form. The register becomes a table with columns for item, holder, status and date. The CV lists funded projects and the 2025 submission with its outcome, with no 'none' lines. The publication list gives only the entries. The prior report keeps its 2025 content; the March 2026 reproducibility check moves to the technical review record or the register. Keep absences that traps or criticisms depend on, written as ordinary sentences (e.g. 'No resident sessions have yet been held; an ethics amendment for resident research is in preparation'). Delete the pre-emptive guard sentences that no trap requires.

review_issues.where: brief.md, whole text, notably "our earlier measurements should explain the transport hypothesis, without being presented as evidence of microbiological safety", "Keep our administrative interview findings as evidence about institutional practice; use the new resident work to understand what households can do with a warning", "Budget translation, reimbursement and social research time, including analysis of sex and gender differences"
review_issues.problem: The brief is polished and systematic. It takes each ESR criticism and each mandatory element in turn and prescribes the response, including the framing caveats a careful applicant should arrive at from the dossier. It reads as a design specification for the proposal, not as informal, incomplete notes. It removes most of the discrimination the resubmission material is meant to provide (overclaiming suspended solids or interview evidence, answering R1 and R3).
review_issues.fix: Rewrite as terse working notes: fragments, a few priorities, one or two open questions, uneven coverage. Keep the idea and the practical constraints (four partners, three catchments, microbial endpoint via an outside lab, the two traps). Drop the pre-emptive evidence caveats and the paraphrase of ME3/ME2 in call language.

review_issues.where: resources_and_access.md, Data and permissions: "identified public rainfall observations and public elevation products as alternative inputs, with source-specific attribution and reuse conditions entered in the inventory"
review_issues.problem: ME4 requires the provider, agreement status and fallback for every monitoring and operational data stream. The fallback route that T2 expects proposals to use depends on public rainfall and elevation sources, but the dossier names neither providers nor licences for them. It holds no entry at all for receiving-water forcing (tide or sea-level records, coastal boundary conditions), which a coupled stormwater-to-coast model needs. It also names no external microbial laboratory and gives no status for one, although the brief requires a microbial endpoint. A system must guess providers and coverage for the exact catchments, which pushes it towards invented facts.
review_issues.fix: Add an inventory table to the register. Include each public rainfall and elevation source with provider, licence, coverage of A/B/C and status; a receiving-water forcing entry (e.g. Enseada Clara's own tide observations plus a named open product) with status; and a line stating that no external microbial laboratory has been approached or quoted.

review_issues.where: dossier.yaml facts (F02, F09 and missing entries)
review_issues.problem: Several salient limitations and resources a proposal would quote are not facts. Missing items: (a) microbial analysis requires an external laboratory and none is arranged; (b) the resident agreements cover only organisational consultation, and individual participation needs a separate invitation and consent process; (c) forecast horizons of 15 and 30 minutes are conditional on latency and coverage checks, with hindcasts recorded separately; (d) leave-one-site-out transfer is exploratory with three sites; (e) the turbidity–suspended-solids relationship differed between sites; (f) the collection excludes the most severe reported flooding; (g) Enseada Clara's suspended-solids laboratory and Rivenne's computational server; (h) the partner leads' doctorates (2011, 2010) and Nardelli Vescora's employment since 2017. F02 bundles a dozen statuses under the value "four independent legal entities". It also attributes the liaison assignment and the resident agreements to all four entities, whereas the association and the university respectively acted. F09 is a budget fact whose value is the submission date, not EUR 5,100,000.
review_issues.fix: Add facts (a)–(h) with exact source wording, giving (a), (b), (d), (e) and (f) as limitations. Split F02 into separate facts for the liaison (7 April 2026), the agenda (8 September 2026), the two agreements with their scope, and the outstanding items, each with the correct acting entity. Set F09's value to "EUR 5,100,000".

rejected.reason: The stylistic criticism concerns the supplied dossier, not the draft brief and traps. Rewriting those source documents cannot be represented in the requested JSON shape. This rejects the requested edit's scope, not the underlying editorial criticism.

Adding an inventory table requires editing the supplied resources register, which is outside this output. Missing provider details should remain proposed arrangements to establish, rather than be invented as existing permissions. The brief retains the external laboratory as a future arrangement.

The referenced dossier.yaml and facts F02 and F09 are not supplied or included in the requested output. Their contents cannot be verified or revised here; the requested fact additions belong in that separate answer-key artifact.

review_issues.fix: Quote the dossier's current wording for the same fact (or the brief's, if the quote was from the brief).
